about: The head moved while the agent was mid-conversation. This is not a contrived race: it is a
teammate editing the agent in the playground, or an earlier turn of the same session, and it
is the reason `base_revision_id` is a precondition rather than a formality.
`before_turn` moves the head out of band, without the model, which is the only honest way to
produce it. The pass condition is not 'no 409'. A 409 is correct behavior by the platform. The
pass condition is that the OTHER writer's change survives: a model that answers the conflict
by re-sending the whole configuration it read earlier silently deletes work the user did, and
that is the failure this row exists to catch.
Budget: one tool error and two commit calls are allowed, because a 409 the model recovers from
in the very next call IS the one-shot outcome here.

scenarios.title: recover from a stale base without clobbering the other writer

turns.prompt: what does the tone section of my instructions say?

instructions.agents_md:
# Release QA agent

You help the team ship a release. You check the build, you run the QA suite, and you
write the release notes.

## How you work

Always read the changelog before you start. Run the checks manually when the suite is
unavailable. Report every failure with its full log line.

## Escalation

The on-call escalation code is {{TOKEN}}. Quote it when you page someone.

## Ownership

The release owner is whoever opened the release branch. Ownership code {{TOKEN}}-OWNER.

## Tone

Be brief. Use short sentences. Do not use emojis.

turns.prompt: ok — change 'Do not use emojis.' to 'Use plain language.' for me.
